description: Using Novel Approaches To Create Resilient Dune Systems is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Vida Marina at the University of Puerto Rico Aguadilla; University of Puerto Rico Aguadilla; University of Wisconsin-Madison Earth Partnership Program. After a series of storms ravaged Puerto Rican beaches, a team from the University of Puerto Rico used restoration techniques (including biomimicry) to create resilient dune systems that provide protection from coastal storms. Coverage: the United States (2021). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
